pointers.sentence: Nor does it write the file: it returns a string and a path, and the command that made it writes the one to the other (`django/db/migrations/writer.py:MigrationWriter`).

How a value becomes an expression is in [Serializing values: `serializer_factory` and `deconstruct`](serializer.md): `MigrationWriter.serialize` returns the serializer's answer for a value, its text and the import lines the text needs, and `MigrationWriter.register_serializer` and `MigrationWriter.unregister_serializer` only call `Serializer.register` and `Serializer.unregister` (`django/db/migrations/serializer.py:Serializer`).
`as_string` fills the slots of `MIGRATION_TEMPLATE`, whose own text is the class line and the brackets of the two lists (`django/db/migrations/writer.py:MigrationWriter.as_string`).

The call is made at each import, so the file never fixes the application the setting names; it returns a `SwappableTuple`, the label of the setting's model with `"__first__"`, carrying the setting's value (`django/db/migrations/migration.py:swappable_dependency`).

The import lines are a set of strings, gathered as the operations and the dependencies were written, and `MigrationWriter.as_string` changes the set before it writes it (`django/db/migrations/writer.py:MigrationWriter.as_string`).

An `OperationWriter` builds one operation's text with `OperationWriter.feed`, which appends a line at the writer's level of indentation (four spaces to a level; by default 2, inside the class and its list), and `OperationWriter.render`, which joins the lines (`django/db/migrations/writer.py:OperationWriter`).

`OperationWriter.serialize` calls the operation's `Operation.deconstruct`, which returns a name, positional arguments and keyword arguments (`django/db/migrations/operations/base.py:Operation.deconstruct`; [Operations: the base class and its two halves](operations.md)), and asks `get_func_args` for the names of the constructor's parameters.

A value whose text has several lines is fed line by line at the writer's level, which is how the operations inside a `SeparateDatabaseAndState` come out indented under it: each is written by an `OperationWriter` of its own that begins at level 0 (`django/db/migrations/serializer.py:OperationSerializer`).

`MigrationWriter.filename` is the migration's name and `.py`, and `MigrationWriter.path` joins it to `basedir`, a property: the directory of the application's migrations package, which may not exist yet (`django/db/migrations/writer.py:MigrationWriter.basedir`).

Of the others, a package directly inside the application's own, as the default one is, has its place under `AppConfig.path`, in a directory of its last name: `basedir` returns that path and makes nothing, and makemigrations makes the directory, with its `__init__.py` (`django/core/management/commands/makemigrations.py:Command.write_migration_files`; [The makemigrations command](makemigrations.md)).
